title: "Refine Clusters in Spatial Transcriptomics Objects"
output: rmarkdown::html_vignette
vignette: >
  %\VignetteIndexEntry{Refine Clusters in Spatial Transcriptomics Objects}
  %\VignetteEngine{knitr::rmarkdown}
  %\VignetteEncoding{UTF-8}
---

`RunFiberMargin()` refines an existing clustering stored in a Seurat,
SpatialExperiment, or Giotto Suite object. It uses coordinates and cluster
labels, not gene expression, images, or embedding coordinates. It returns the
same type of object with a new metadata column, `FiberMargin_clusters` by
default. The input cluster column and active Seurat identities are unchanged.

## A reproducible example

The examples below use the same two simulated tissue sections. The expression
matrix is a placeholder required to construct the objects; FiberMargin never
uses its values.

```{r setup}
library(fibermargin)

sim <- simulate_gradient_regions(n = 480L, minority = 0.20,
                                 samples = 2L, seed = 42L)
xy <- sim$xy
colnames(xy) <- c("x", "y")
ids <- sprintf("spot%03d", seq_len(nrow(xy)))
rownames(xy) <- ids
metadata <- data.frame(clusters = sim$labels, sample_id = sim$samples,
                       row.names = ids)
counts <- matrix(1L, nrow = 2L, ncol = length(ids),
                 dimnames = list(c("gene1", "gene2"), ids))

refined <- RefineMargin(xy, metadata$clusters, metadata$sample_id, workers = 1L)
data.frame(
  initial_accuracy = mean(metadata$clusters == sim$truth),
  refined_accuracy = mean(refined == sim$truth),
  sites_changed = sum(attr(refined, "changed"))
)
```

The simulated reference labels are used only to score the result. On a real
specimen without a reference, the number of edits can be inspected, but it is
not a measure of accuracy. The object examples below run when their optional
framework packages are installed; the matrix example runs without them.

```{r framework-availability, include=FALSE}
have_spe <- requireNamespace("SpatialExperiment", quietly = TRUE) &&
  requireNamespace("SummarizedExperiment", quietly = TRUE)
have_seurat <- requireNamespace("Seurat", quietly = TRUE) &&
  requireNamespace("SeuratObject", quietly = TRUE)
have_giotto <- requireNamespace("GiottoClass", quietly = TRUE)
```

## SpatialExperiment

Specify the column in `colData()` that contains the input labels.
`RunFiberMargin()` takes coordinates from `spatialCoords()` and uses
`sample_id` to keep the two sections independent. If the object stores three
spatial columns, all varying axes are used.

```{r spatialexperiment, eval=have_spe}
spe <- SpatialExperiment::SpatialExperiment(
  assays = list(counts = counts), spatialCoords = xy, colData = metadata
)
spe <- RunFiberMargin(spe, cluster.column = "clusters", workers = 1L)
table(input = spe$clusters, refined = spe$FiberMargin_clusters)
stopifnot(identical(as.character(spe$FiberMargin_clusters), as.character(refined)))
```

## Seurat

By default the wrapper uses active identities. Set `cluster.column` to
read a different metadata column. The coordinates are spot positions for
Visium objects and cell centroids for fields of view. Each image is an
independent coordinate system, even if different images have overlapping
coordinate ranges.

```{r seurat, eval=have_seurat}
seu <- SeuratObject::CreateSeuratObject(
  counts = methods::as(counts, "CsparseMatrix"), meta.data = metadata
)
SeuratObject::Idents(seu) <- "clusters"
for (i in seq_along(unique(metadata$sample_id))) {
  section <- unique(metadata$sample_id)[i]
  keep <- metadata$sample_id == section
  name <- paste0("section", i)
  seu[[name]] <- SeuratObject::CreateFOV(
    as.data.frame(xy[keep, , drop = FALSE]), type = "centroids",
    assay = "RNA", key = paste0(name, "_")
  )
}

initial_idents <- SeuratObject::Idents(seu)
seu <- RunFiberMargin(seu, workers = 1L)
table(input = initial_idents, refined = seu[[]]$FiberMargin_clusters)
stopifnot(identical(initial_idents, SeuratObject::Idents(seu)),
          identical(as.character(seu[[]]$FiberMargin_clusters), as.character(refined)))
```

To refine only one image, give its name and a different output column.
The other observations retain their input labels in the new column.
If two images contain the same cell IDs, select a non-overlapping set of
images explicitly.

```{r seurat-one-image, eval=have_seurat}
seu <- RunFiberMargin(seu, cluster.column = "clusters", images = "section1",
                      output.column = "section1_refined", workers = 1L)
other <- metadata$sample_id != unique(metadata$sample_id)[1L]
stopifnot(identical(seu[[]]$section1_refined[other], metadata$clusters[other]))
```

## Giotto Suite

Specify a cell metadata column containing the existing clustering. The
wrapper matches locations to metadata by cell ID, uses `sdimz` when it
is present, and writes the result to the selected spatial unit and feature
type. This example only constructs a small fixture. It does not need a
Python-based Giotto workflow.

```{r giotto, eval=have_giotto}
locations <- data.frame(cell_ID = ids, sdimx = xy[, "x"], sdimy = xy[, "y"])
cell_metadata <- data.frame(cell_ID = ids, clusters = metadata$clusters,
                            sample_id = metadata$sample_id)
gio <- (function() {
  old <- options(giotto.use_conda = FALSE, giotto.no_python_warn = TRUE)
  on.exit(options(old))
  # The GiottoClass constructor may report a deprecation in its own internals.
  suppressWarnings(GiottoClass::createGiottoObject(
    expression = counts, spatial_locs = locations,
    cell_metadata = cell_metadata, cores = 1L
  ))
})()
gio <- RunFiberMargin(gio, cluster.column = "clusters", workers = 1L)
gio_meta <- GiottoClass::getCellMetadata(gio, output = "data.table")
table(input = gio_meta[["clusters"]], refined = gio_meta[["FiberMargin_clusters"]])
stopifnot(identical(
  as.character(gio_meta[["FiberMargin_clusters"]][match(ids, gio_meta[["cell_ID"]])]),
  as.character(refined)
))
```

For a Giotto object with multiple location layers, pass `location` and, where
necessary, `spat_unit` or `feat_type`.

## Before running on your data

- **Keep coordinate systems separate.** Supply `sample.column` when specimen
  identifiers are stored under a name other than `sample_id`. Use measured
  z coordinates for a volume; do not encode separate slides as artificial z
  values to join unrelated coordinate systems.
- **Choose a new output column.** Existing metadata columns are never
  overwritten. Reuse the original object or give a different `output.column`
  for a second run.
- **Inspect changes.** A label can disappear after refinement. For candidate
  labels, repair margins, and per-specimen summaries, call `RefineMargin()`
  with the same coordinates, assignments, and specimen identifiers.

```{r diagnostics}
attr(refined, "labels_changed")
attr(refined, "removed_classes")
```

See `?RunFiberMargin` for the complete interface and `?RefineMargin` for the
meaning of each diagnostic.
